descriptionChirho: To ask a question or make an inquiry, seeking information or an answer. Covers perfective 'we asked', participle 'asks', and simple past 'asked.' English 'we-asked/asks/asked', Spanish 'preguntamos/pregunta/ha-preguntado' (we asked/asks/has asked), Hindi 'humne-puche/puchta-hai/puchi' (we asked/asks/asked), Arabic 'sa'alnahum/yas'alu/yas'al' (we asked them/he asks/he asked), Korean 'muleotda/munneun/mutji' (asked/asking/asking), Swahili 'tuliwauliza/anauliza/kuuliza' (we asked them/he asks/to ask). All share the core interrogative sense of seeking information.

To make a request or demand of someone, asking for something to be given or done rather than merely inquiring. English 'asks-of-you' (request directed at someone), Spanish 'os-pida' (may request of you), Hindi 'mange tumse' (demand from you), Arabic 'yatlubuhu-minkum' (he requests it from you, using talaba = demand/request, distinct from sa'ala = ask), Korean 'yoguhada-neohui-ege' (to demand of you), Swahili 'atawaomba' (he will request of them, using omba = request/beg). The shift from sa'ala to talaba in Arabic confirms a distinct 'request/demand' sense.
